note: ADR 0009's four rules, judged headless by driving the CLI on scratch copy design-1001 with its own WALKDOWN_HOME; an undrawn screen probe-undrawn was added to the copy's storyboard only.

results.reasoning: With probe-undrawn at prototype: null and nothing filed, lint names it: 'screen has no design and no open design request' (probe-2, step 4). Filing a request with thread new --screen cleared it (step 7, only the unrelated app-ref tie warning remained). After both requests were settled, an open feedback note n-0339 on the same screen did not clear it and the warning came back (probe-4, 10b), so a non-request note does not count and an ended request stops counting. One aside: the scratch status lists many 'cover' items because the copy has no checks/ tree; that is the copy, not this rule.

With design unset the status report heads the request 'DESIGN QUEUE — for the designer' (probe-2, step 8). With design.by: agent it reads 'DESIGN QUEUE — for the design agent, never the agent building the app', and lint is silent on design.by (probe-3, step 11). With design.by: robot lint errors under [config] naming person and agent as allowed values, and status falls back to the designer's queue (step 12). I did not probe design.by: person spelled out; it takes the same branch as unset in designBy().

thread new with no anchor is refused, exit 2, saying to name --rule or --screen; an unknown screen is refused by name (probe-1). thread new --screen probe-undrawn with no reason wrote n-0338 with anchor.screen only, no rule, reason: request, and lint's drift warning for that screen disappeared (probe-2, steps 6-7). Given --reason feedback on the same screen, n-0339 carried feedback and did not clear drift (probe-3/4). A note filed with --rule and no reason (n-0341) got the existing person default, feedback, not request, so the default is confined to screen-only threads.

The scratch report lists a DESIGN QUEUE ahead of the AGENT QUEUE, each item saying what to do: 'draw probe-undrawn — design request n-0338' under design, and 'address n-0339 — open note', 'address n-0341 (rule) — open note', 'cover <rule> — demands checks, and no check claims it', and 'judge <rule>' under the agent (probe-2, probe-3 step 9 and below). The request never appears as an agent item; the only other mentions of it are the drift summary and the recent-threads list. Once both requests were settled the design queue disappeared and the feedback note stayed with the agent (probe-4). Each item sits in exactly one queue.
